item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is much closer to the frozen contract: it adds only the requested convenience API, reuses the established multipart helper, and leaves retry and association machinery alone. Its main defect is duplicating Add instead of routing through it.","reasons":["B adds the exact Upload signature and uses multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), producing a buffered, replayable multipart body with the required field and filename.","B preserves FilesService.Add implementation and existing FilesOption behavior, while A changes global RawClient body/retry/closing semantics and therefore changes Add behavior despite the explicit scope restriction.","A directly violates the prohibition on association fields by adding seven typed association options, raw form values, validation machinery, and NewFileWithFields.","A introduces broad retry/request-body machinery affecting Raw.Do and unrelated upload paths, expressly outside the requested scope and substantially increasing review risk relative to B's focused patch mentioned in contract to avoid unrelated machinery changes refactor/retry machinery."],"risks_a":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request/response logic.","The new seek-based GetBody closure reuses and mutates one reader, adding subtle global transport and ownership semantics beyond the task.","No visible Upload test covers a failing source reader; its retry test also uses a seekable strings.Reader rather than streamed content."],"risks_b":["Upload also bypasses FilesService.Add, violating the contract's required single path for option handling, decoding, and errors.","Visible tests omit empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader failure cases.","The retry test uses strings.NewReader and does not set RetryAllMethods, so it does not closely model the reported streamed os.File configuration."]}
